Maya (CS): quick digest from this week's onboarding demos with three pilots. common asks below — customers asked for concrete exports they can hand to procurement.
Maya (CS): summary bullets: per-route cost control, auto-detect stale embeddings, CSV with prioritized asks + customer quote, small UI to tag route as experimental.
Maya (CS): verbatim: "We need a switch to stop running embeddings for low-touch routes. It's burning $800/mo in pilot credits." — OrionHealth
Maya (CS): verbatim: "Our SREs re-upload weekly and keep creating duplicate vectors — is there a way to detect staleness?" — ParkCo
Maya (CS): verbatim: "Export with severity + renewal-impact would speed our handover to product." — TridentRetail
Omar (Product): thanks. can you share the rough cost delta per pilot and which renewal talks are affected?
Maya (CS): OrionHealth flagged renewal as contingent on cost reduction. they estimated $800/mo extra. ParkCo wants SLA for index freshness but not blocking. TridentRetail: export would speed their internal review but not blocking.
Priya (Solutions): short-term workaround: add a metadata tag on routes called "experimental" and filter on support exports. we already have route tags in the support DB. low effort.
Sam (Eng-ML): technical note: hard-disable of embedding compute interacts with batching and KV cache invalidation. if you disable compute for a route, we need to decide whether queries fallback to a cached embedding or to a cheap semantic fallback. toggling also affects throughput math.
Sam (Eng-ML): alternative: keep compute on but add a sampling policy + quota per route. or a soft-toggle that marks embeddings as "skip-hotpath" so they don't get batched with latency-sensitive traffic.
Omar (Product): propose triage: 1) Export CSV with tags + severity + renewal_flag (fast). 2) Route tagging UX & support export filter (fast). 3) Embedding staleness detector + TTL policy (medium). 4) Per-route hard-disable toggle (investigate).
Maya (CS): export will help procurement packets this week. can you include these columns in CSV: account, route_name, ask_summary, severity(P0/P1/P2), renewal_risk(yes/no), customer_quote, est_cost_delta_usd, date_reported, reporter
ExportBot: created ad-hoc export job job_id=exp_1775123456_v1 ; output s3://cs-exports/1775123456_maya_export.csv :rocket:
Priya (Solutions): i'll wire the route tag filter into the support export endpoint. ETA Wed EOD for a first pass.
Sam (Eng-ML): for staleness detection naive heuristic: last_vector_update_ts vs last_query_ts and vector drift > 0.15 cosine over sample window. we can prototype in indexer; small-medium effort.
Omar (Product): Sam, any rough engineering cost estimate for TTL prototype?
Sam (Eng-ML): estimate 2-3 sprints for robust detector + alerting. prototype could be 1 sprint if we accept sampling and no UI.
Maya (CS): marking OrionHealth as renewal-at-risk. i'll DM finance for exact spend to attach to the RICE card.
Omar (Product): I'll create RICE entries for the four items and tag you, Maya, for impact numbers. scheduling 30m sync Thu 9am PT to triage.
Maya (CS): great. will collect procurement docs and paste the OrionHealth billing extract in this thread when I have it.
ExportBot: export finished: s3://cs-exports/1775123456_maya_export.csv (contains 9 rows) :white_check_mark:
Priya (Solutions): posted PR to add "experimental" filter to support export endpoint. link: https://git.internal/redwood/support-export/pull/198
Maya (CS): thanks team — this should make the procurement handoff way faster. :thumbsup:
